title: docs+skills: three authoring pages still say a system-elevated hook, action body or flow bypasses every check; the four identity-assignment objects are refused (system-context.mdx row 1b, #25653)
body:
Filing gate ①: a product defect with a named location. These are author-facing pages that state a rule the runtime no longer keeps. This is a follow-up owed by landed work (#25653's run-time half on `main`, and its save-time half in PR #26430). Filed by `domain:spec` seat 1 (#6017, session `session_01WGufzfhobWEgUUrjz4rrbh`) from contract review 6433419685 item 12. ⛔ Not a claim.

**Business reason:** an app author reads that `runAs: 'system'` (or an action body) is "full-access" and "bypasses row- and field-level security". They write a hook or action that assigns a position, a permission set, an invitation or a membership, and it is refused at run time (`PERMISSION_DENIED`). After PR #26430 lands, it is also refused at save time when the body names the object as a literal. The pages tell the author to expect the opposite of what happens, and they omit the remedy the refusal names.

**Reader who acts:** the lane triage names. The items span two lanes: `content/docs/**` and `skills/**` (Tier H). This card carries no `domain:*`; triage splits or routes it.

## Where

At `origin/main`, read 2026-10-27:
- `content/docs/automation/hooks.mdx:157`: the `'system'` row says "elevated: a full-access, RLS-bypassing system principal. Row and field permissions do not apply…"
- `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx:443-445`: "An action body and a registered handler both run **elevated**: `ctx.api` and `ctx.engine` carry `isSystem`, so they bypass row- and field-level security by design…"
- `skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md:164-191`: the `runAs: 'system'` guidance ("the trusted-writer channel", "Elevate the write, not the flow") never says that writes to the four objects are refused.

The rule is already written once, correctly, at `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` row **1b**. Each page above owes one sentence plus the link: a governed write (insert, update, delete, transfer, restore, purge) to `sys_user_position`, `sys_user_permission_set`, `sys_invitation` or `sys_member` from app-authored system automation is refused, and the remedy is the delegated-administration door that the refusal message names. The skill also owes an eval prompt per its package's convention.

## Also carried here (from the #26430 dev report, out of that card's scope)

- `FlowSchema` has no save-time twin of #26430's body check. A `runAs: 'system'` flow's data node that names one of the four objects is refused only at run time (`18.flow-run-as-system-identity-assignment-write-refused` is the run-time entry). Decide whether a save-time refusal is owed. That would be a spec narrowing, so it moves to the spec lane if yes.
- The four-object set and the prescription text are duplicated between `packages/spec/src/identity/identity-assignment-body-writes.ts` (from #26430) and `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/flow-system-identity-write-refusal.ts`. One should import the other, so the two cannot drift.

Dedupe: an issue search for "system elevation bypass docs identity-assignment hooks.mdx actions.mdx" (open and closed) found no card naming these pages. #25653 and #26430 name the spec and runtime halves only.
